sent:
Maya,

What’s costing you leads: two doors (Book a call vs Enquire/Quick Brief) plus early asks (deadline/budget). When the calendar shows no times, high‑intent visitors stall. Your wins and metrics are strong—use them earlier to earn the click.

Do these first:
1) One primary CTA site‑wide: “Get a cost + start date.” Route hero and packages to one slim form.
2) Slim form: email + brand URL + goal (e.g., “4 UGC videos to test 6 hooks”). Ask budget/deadline after you reply.
3) Swap the calendar gate for “Request times.” Keep calls, but propose two slots by email when asked.

Then tighten:
4) Put three work thumbnails with your own metrics (e.g., “CTR 1.2%→2.1%,” “5.8% watch‑through,” “4 hooks, 2 winners”) in the first screen; link to Work.
5) Make package CTAs consistent: “Get this package,” prefilled in the slim form.
6) Put usage/rights as a single line by the price; keep the detail in FAQs.
7) Rename packages to outcomes where possible (e.g., “Test 6 hooks in 10–14 days”).
8) Keep the Free UGC Brief Template as a secondary path; don’t split the hero’s job.
9) Add a visible fallback under the primary CTA: “Prefer a call? Request times—no calendar.”
10) Echo your 48‑hour reply promise beside the main CTA and on submit.

Quick tests for this week:
- Hero CTA: “Get a cost + start date” vs current. Measure form completions.
- Proof placement: hero thumbnails vs current. Measure form starts.
- Form friction: slim form vs Quick Brief. Measure completion rate and 48‑hour replies sent.

If useful, I can send paste‑in hero copy and the slim form fields.
